producer_report.summary: Root cause: `[budget] job_usd` was never required to cover the reader, every planning round, the producer and the verifier, and nothing refused an athena.toml that set it too low. The runtime `preflight` already existed and only fires when a job starts. The new piece is a refusal where an unaffordable budget enters the repository. In config.rs I added the one sum of the stage caps (`Config::planning_usd`, `critic_usd`, `run_usd`, `budget_required`), `ConfigError::BudgetBelowReserve` and `Config::check_budget()`. The error names `[budget] job_usd` and the shortfall. `Config::parse` and `validate` are unchanged, so history walks and recovery commands still load a short file. reading.rs `budget_reserve` now takes every stage's sum from those helpers, so there is no second hand-written sum in non-test code. In admission.rs, when a candidate changes athena.toml and the schema is not changing, a file that parses but fails `check_budget` gets its own `configuration` violation. CHANGELOG.md has the Unreleased/Fixed entry naming the root cause and the three jobs. I did not run the full `cargo test`; Athena runs it.

checks_run.note: 19 passed, including shipped_budget_covers_the_reserve, required_budget_follows_the_configured_caps, a_job_usd_below_the_stage_caps_is_a_configuration_violation and the runtime BudgetShort pin tests
The first run failed only on my new admission test, because its 12.00 control case was an identical file and the helper's empty commit failed. I changed the control to an '# edited' copy and reran.

I did not run it with the check stubbed out.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: the shipped athena.toml still parses and shipped_budget_covers_the_reserve passes; a test changes a cap (planner_usd or max_rounds) and shows the required budget changes with no other code change.

It also checks the refusal at the requirement minus 0.01 and acceptance at exactly the requirement.

open_issues: The check runs only when a change to athena.toml is admitted. `Config::parse`, `JobConfig::at` and drain are not changed, so a short head budget that reaches the repository another way is still caught only by the existing runtime preflight, which drain holds as BudgetShort. This follows the plan: a parse-time refusal would break history walks and the recovery commands.
A candidate that changes athena.toml together with crates/athena-data/ (schema_changed) skips the budget check, the same as the existing parse check. The candidate's own athena-data tests judge it.
`Config::check_budget` is public, but the only non-test caller is admission.rs.
The error variant carries a third field `short` beyond the planned `{job_usd, required}`, so the message does not recompute the shortfall.
I did not run the full `cargo test --locked`; Athena runs it.
mistakes: My first admission test used the unchanged base config as the control, which fails in the test helper. Fixed with an edited copy.
learnings: The admission test helper `admit_files` commits the candidate over a base that already holds BASE_CONFIG, so a candidate identical to base makes an empty commit that fails. Use an '# edited' copy for a no-change control.
`Config` has `job_plan: Option<JobPlanConfig>` and `JobPlanConfig` is Copy. Reserve code reads caps through it, and `enabled` matters only at Admission.
The shipped athena.toml needs 10.00 (0.50 + 3 × 1.50 + 5.00) and sets job_usd = 12.00.
